evidence.note: Seven explicit TaskCreate milestones forming a dependency-ordered hierarchy: foundation/storage substrate + audit + tenant seeding first, then SigV4 auth, then data-plane CRUD/multipart/versioning, then policy/notifications/lifecycle, then admin+console API, then console SPA, then a final boto3 test/fix task. Correct foundational-before-dependent ordering, subsystems treated as discrete units.
Milestones marked in_progress then completed in sequence across the entire build, showing a coherent map sustained over the whole horizon rather than abandoned early planning.

Console UI built (task 6) and verified via a dedicated Playwright browser-test track, distinct from the boto3 correctness track (steps 92-150) — the two grading surfaces are scoped as separate tracks.

SigV4 exactness and concurrency (highest-uncertainty foundations) were only exercised by acceptance tests after essentially all code was written, and the entire data plane was lumped into one task rather than gated incrementally — falling short of risk-ordered, per-milestone acceptance checks (anchors 8/10).

reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-sequenced milestone hierarchy (steps 21-27) with foundational auth/storage before dependent features and the console scoped as its own track, and it tracked those milestones to completion across the whole trajectory — clearly above anchor 5 and approaching 8. It stops short of a full 8/10 because there is no stated per-milestone 'done' check (verification was a lumped final task, and the data plane was one omnibus task rather than gated as 'PUT/GET signed before multipart'), and the highest-risk foundations (SigV4, concurrency) were built-then-tested rather than proven earliest, so the level lands at 7.
